extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to NIH (PIs, early-career investigators, grants admins)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and procedural criteria for NIH grant applicants (resubmission vs appeal, timelines, budgeting, overlap rules, special mechanisms like R56/R15). Focused on interactions with Program Officials, Council, and Grants Management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upgrading project role (co-I → MPI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss possibility of changing project role (e.g., from co-Investigator to Multiple PI) with the Program Officer if a linked award is funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a related award (e.g., NHGRI U01) is funded, explore 'upgrading' to MPI with the PO; obtain timeline/next steps from the PO and post updates. Institutional/IC approval and timing/administrative steps will apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited council review criteria (NIAID example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications sent for expedited council (electronic approval en bloc) meet both: rank within payline and no concerns (e.g., human/animal codes) from study section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process happens before every Council meeting. Expedited review does not guarantee immediate award; timing depends on IC practices and available funds. Check with PO for likely award timing (e.g., December/January vs later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal year and award timing (which FY determines payline)
rubrics_metrics.description: FY is determined by the Council/advisory council date: October Council is for the next Federal FY (e.g., October 2021 council = FY2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs can sometimes choose to pay an application in the prior FY if funds allow (late-September awards). Expect awards to depend on when the federal budget is signed; earliest possible award for new FY may be December but often occurs later. Consult your PO for IC-specific behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of a JIT (Just-in-Time) request
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIT request from the GMO/IC typically indicates positive interest in funding but is not a guarantee of award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commons status might not change when GMO processes JIT. After JIT, the application still waits for IC Director/awards office review ('Award prepared' status can last up to a week or more). Do not contact GMO repeatedly (may cause delays); PO can provide context.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to resubmit vs wait (resubmission strategy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether to submit an A1/A0 based on payline prospects, PO advice, reviewer enthusiasm, and other productivity (e.g., new data or manuscripts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PO says 'resubmission is up to you' consider using the cycle to prepare a new project or strengthen supporting publications. If reviewers are not methodologically critical but not enthusiastic, resubmission with substantial new data may be needed; consult trusted colleagues and your PO about study section fit or changing sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal (Request for Reconsideration) considerations and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals must be submitted by the institution (AOR) asking Council to review the fairness of peer review; appeals are intended for substantive/factual errors and are difficult to win.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal timeline: institutional letter → IC/OER/Council decides → if sent back, A1 is re-reviewed (no changes allowed) and the PI cannot submit an A0 while A1 is under re-review. Council will only send back applications if the error likely changed fundability; appeals are a tough bar and can delay progress by a year or more. Consider resubmitting a new A0 rather than appealing in many cases; discuss with PO whether a select-pay/internal advocacy is possible instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of an appeal on future submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you appeal, you cannot submit a new competing application on the same work while the appealed A1 is under re-review; the A1 returns unchanged to the same SRG for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may block submitting an A0 for many months; SRG members will implicitly know an appeal occurred, and reviewers may be reassigned but the panel composition often remains similar. Factor timeline risk into decision to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget percent effort vs salary support
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH does not require percent effort to equal percent of salary requested (you can request $0 salary for 100% effort), but institutions often will not allow that and you cannot claim more salary than percent effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check with your institutional grants/fiscal office about allowable salary/cost-share arrangements; rebudgeting salary post-award is sometimes possible but must follow institutional and NIH rules and may raise cost-share/F&A considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap/duplicative submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that share aims/overlap significantly across multiple submissions are not allowed; overlapping Aims across multiple active submissions can lead to administrative withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying to different ICs or at different times will not avoid NIH detection (they use software to find similar applications). If applications truly address different diseases or use significantly different experimental models, overlap may be avoidable. Consult your PO before submitting potentially overlapping applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transferring applications across ICs and co-funding (R15 example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are usually not allowed to transfer to another IC after review; options include resubmitting as an A1 with the desired IC as primary or requesting transfer before review via PHS Referral Form and cover letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss with POs at both ICs to see if reframing aims to match the target IC mission or requesting transfer before review is feasible. Secondary-IC interest can sometimes lead to transfer if coordinated pre-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 institutional eligibility considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional eligibility for R15 at time of application may be sufficient for award, but loss of eligibility after award could affect renewals and future eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform the PO if institutional eligibility changed after submission; NIH may allow awarding for the submitted period but renewal would be affected. Key personnel changes (unpaid advisory members) can be updated after award with NIH approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: R56 (bridge) award purpose and budget interaction with R01
rubrics_metrics.description: R56 awards typically fund work proposed in Year 1 of an R01 and are intended to provide bridge funds to get preliminary data for a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an R01 competing application is funded while an R56 is active, the remaining R56 balance is applied toward the competing award's approved amount (funds are not additive). R56 timing usually runs through the fiscal year; if the A1 is later funded, R56 funds are folded into the A1 first-year budget up to that year's approved amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting advisory council dates and Commons listings
rubrics_metrics.description: An Advisory Council listing date in eRA Commons may reflect an 'early Oct' Council; October Council generally corresponds to next FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small administrative variations (e.g., August listing for an Oct Council) are not unusual. Council date alone does not fully predict award since ICs may choose to fund early or wait for federal budget; consult PO for likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select-pay/rebuttal practice is optional
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting a PI rebuttal/response to the summary statement is not a required or consistent practice across ICs and is not a reliable indicator of select-pay consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume funding likelihood from the presence or absence of a requested rebuttal. Historically, some ICs began routinely requesting short rebuttals to help POs justify select-pay decisions, but lack of request does not mean no consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Officer (PO) as primary source of IC-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The PO is the best source for IC-specific practices (paylines, select-pay considerations, R56 likelihood, whether an application might be moved between ICs, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact PO for advice on resubmission vs appeal, transfer requests, payline expectations, and whether to prepare brief responses to summary statements. If the PO is unresponsive, escalate (e.g., copy appropriate IC/division contacts) after a reasonable wait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing timelines and when to contact NIH staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative review, GMO processing, and IC Director approvals have variable durations; frequent contact can slow processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect waits of days to weeks during busy periods; avoid unnecessary follow-up that could cause delays. Use PO/GMO contacts judiciously and coordinate institutional submissions (e.g., JIT) through the Grants Management Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimating payline and IC award practices (no public paylines for some mechanisms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs/mechanisms do not publish explicit paylines (e.g., R15) and award decisions may consider programmatic balance in addition to score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RePORTER to see past awards and consult your PO for intuition about likely payline ranges and programmatic factors (e.g., avoiding clustering awards in one subfield).
